text: A local variable captured by a lambda must never be assigned after initialisation. Java describes such a variable as effectively ___ .
explanation: The reason is a lifetime problem: a local lives in a stack frame that may be gone before the lambda runs, so the value is copied in — and once it is a copy, permitting assignment would make the copy silently disagree with the original. JavaScript captures the variable itself, which is why closures over a loop counter used to all see the final value, a trap Java's restriction has no equivalent of.
